theme.title: Beyond the arc
theme.subtitle: The three-pointer, 1979 to today
theme.recap: It took the NBA years to use the three: the first record was eight in a game and the first 100-three season came in 1988.

questions.prompt: Away from the corners, how far is the NBA three-point arc from the center of the basket, in feet?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: in the National Basketball Association (NBA) the arc is 23 feet 9 inches (7.24 m) from the center of the basket

funFacts.text: The three-point rule debuted in the short-lived American Basketball League before the NBA ever adopted it.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the newly formed American Basketball League (ABL) became the first basketball league to institute the rule in 1961

funFacts.text: The ABA paired three-pointers with dunks in its marketing to offer fans a different kind of basketball.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: During the 1970s, the ABA used the three-point shot, along with the slam dunk, as a marketing tool to compete with the NBA

funFacts.text: The NBA introduced the arc on a trial basis in 1979; Boston's Chris Ford made the league's first official three.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Chris Ford of the Boston Celtics is credited with making the first three-point shot in NBA history on October 12, 1979

questions.prompt: Rick Barry set the first NBA record for threes in a game in February 1980. How many did he make?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Barry would later set the original 3-point record at 8 in a single game on February 9, 1980 against the Utah Jazz.

funFacts.text: Barry's final season overlapped with Larry Bird's Boston debut; both were present for an early NBA three.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Rick Barry of the Houston Rockets, in his final season, also made one in the same game

funFacts.text: Julius Erving made the only three of the entire 1980 NBA Finals, showing how rare the shot still was.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: In the 1980 NBA Finals, Julius Erving made the only three of the series

funFacts.text: In one 1980 Finals game, neither team even attempted a three-pointer.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: in Game 4, neither team attempted a single shot beyond the arc

questions.prompt: In 1987–88 Danny Ainge became the first player with 100 threes in a season. How many did he make?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Danny Ainge was the first player to make over 100 three-pointers in a season in 1988, scoring 148 that season.

funFacts.text: Dale Ellis later became the first NBA player to hit a thousand career threes.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: In 1994, Ellis became the first NBA player to reach 1,000 career three-pointers

funFacts.text: John Starks was the first NBA player to make more than two hundred threes in one season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: In 1995, John Starks became the first player to make over 200 three-pointers in a season

funFacts.text: The three-pointer first appeared at the Olympics in Seoul, four years after FIBA introduced it.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: FIBA, introduced the three-point line in 1984, at 6.25 m (20 ft 6 in), and it made its Olympic debut in 1988

questions.prompt: Reggie Miller retired in 2005 as the career leader in threes. How many had he made?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: eventually retiring with a record 2,560 three-pointers made.

funFacts.text: Miller overtook Dale Ellis for the career lead in 1997, well before the modern three-point explosion.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: In 1997, Miller surpassed Ellis as the NBA's all-time leader in three-pointers

funFacts.text: During Miller's career, the NBA briefly shortened the three-point line for three seasons before restoring it.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: For three seasons beginning in 1994–95, the NBA attempted to address decreased scoring by shortening the distance

funFacts.text: The NBA's later three-point revolution is often credited to Stephen Curry and his unusually deep attempts.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Stephen Curry, who is credited with revolutionizing the game by inspiring teams to more heavily employ the three-point shot

questions.prompt: In a double-overtime game on December 1, 2016, how many threes did the Warriors and Rockets attempt combined?
questions.context: Warriors vs Houston Rockets · 2016–17 · double overtime

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Most combined three-point attempts in a single game: 88

funFacts.text: Golden State and Houston each took exactly 44 attempts from beyond the arc in their double-overtime shootout.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Both the Warriors and the Houston Rockets took 44 attempts each on December 1, 2016

funFacts.text: Golden State also became the first team to have four different players make four threes in a single game that season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: First team to have four players hit four three-pointers in a single game

funFacts.text: That Warriors roster sent Curry, Durant, Thompson and Draymond Green to the same All-Star Game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Kevin Durant, Stephen Curry, Klay Thompson and Draymond Green were all named to the All-Star Game
